description: Part IOverview:In the first part of the final project, you will set up a complex scene by loading from two simple file formatsâ€”OBJ models accompanied by MTL material files. You will then apply lighting and texturing. When it is done, your scene will consist of a lit and colored car sitting on a lit and colored road next to a lit and textured stop sign, illuminated by a lit and colored streetlamp.Part 1-1: Setting your SceneThe first step is to review the starter code for this project. It contains a Model and a Face class and a series of calls that take in OBJ and MTL files and parses them into Model objects. Make sure you understand what this code is doing and what it returns so that you know how to use it in your program. You are welcome (but not required) to make any modifications to this code that you see fit. If you see any errors in this starter code or have any suggestions for improvement, let the instructor know.The starter code produces several console.log() statements that allow you to look at everything that has been processed from the files. You should study these statements to understand how the data in the Model class is organized. In particular, node how Model has an array of Face instances that contain all of the vertices, normals, and texture coordinates for each face in that model. The faces have all been triangulated for you, so you can just pass them directly into the vertex shader (either one face at a time or all at once) to draw your mesh using gl.TRIANGLES. Each face also has a corresponding material field that references one of the materials in the diffuseMap and specularMap fields in Model. You can use this information to look up the appropriate values for your lighting calculations on that face.Once you are comfortable with the above information, you should then render your models in a simple view to verify that your program is working. (HINT: Start with the stop sign, since it's the simplest mesh.) You will then want to set up your scene as shown in the demo video (you will incorporate the bunny in a later step). description: I am writing to request your assistance in a data-related task that involves populating a CSV file with essential indicator information.### Guide for Filling Out the Indicator Information CSV File#### 1. ID_Indicators_Information- **Description**: Assign a unique, consecutive ID number to each row/indicator.- **Example**: If the last filled row has ID 10, the next row should have ID 11.#### 2. Indicator Name- **Description**: Enter the official name of the trading indicator.- **Example**: Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD).#### 3. Buffers- **Description**: Enter the buffer values associated with the indicator. Buffers are data arrays storing different values calculated by the indicator.- **Example**: If an indicator has two lines (like MACD), it might have two buffers, one for each line.#### 6. Notes- **Description**: Add any additional comments or observations about the indicator.- **Example**: 'This indicator works well in a trending market'.#### 7. We are keen to work with someone who is not only looking for the immediate task at hand but is also interested in growing with us and contributing to our future projects.Your expertise, dedication, and innovation on this project could make you an integral part of our ongoing journey. title: Crypto data integration
description: For clarity and precision, the project involves integrating and automating data retrieval from the Bitget API v2 for cryptocurrency market analysis, with the workflow divided into three main sections: Historical, Recent, and Live data fetching.Historical Data Fetching:Get History Transactions: Utilizes the endpoint GET /api/v2/mix/market/fills-history to retrieve historical transaction data, which is then aggregated into 1-minute Open, High, Low, Close (OHLC) intervals with summed volumes. This information is also exported to the SQLite database and is fully operational.Recent Data Fetching:The challenge arises in the Recent section, where the objective is to fill the data gap between the last entry in the database and the present moment. The start time for data fetching is determined by the timestamp of the last database record (for example, if the last record is at 2024-02-16 18:31:00, fetching would commence from 2024-02-16 18:32:00), with the end time being the current time when the script is executed. This involves using the GET /api/v2/mix/market/candles endpoint for candlestick data and potentially a similar approach for transaction data through GET /api/v2/mix/market/fills. The fetched data for this period is then exported to the database. I've got some files working but not accurate and I'm running out of time.Live Data Fetching:The live data component is already set up with a WebSocket connection that streams candlestick and public trade transactions, data directly exported into the same database.Required Integration and Automation:The project now needs a cohesive mechanism that ensures synchronization between the Recent and Live data sections. Specifically:- Upon execution, the Python script should first address the Recent data fetching by updating the database with the latest data up to the current moment.- Once the database is current, the script should automatically transition to the Live data streaming via WebSocket to continue the data update in real time.This integrated approach ensures that there is no gap in the data stored in the database, providing a seamless transition from historical to real-time data analysis. Start by evaluating the wearable sensors' accuracy independently, then assess the impact of integrating both types of sensors on accuracy. This is the kind of format and approach I envision for my own thesis eventually.I'd like you to concentrate specifically on the data analysis. title: Evaluating the Quality of Machine-generated Explanations
description: IntroductionAuthor attribution is the task of identifying the author of a given text based on the writing style. In this study, you will evaluate the quality of explanations generated by machine learning models that justify their decision on specific tasks of author attribution. The task consists of two phases: Phase 1 and Phase 2. In the following, we will explain each.Note: Because a portion of the data comes from social media posts, it is possible that you come across potentially distressing content or ideas. However, this content might not be extreme and can be found in public social media. By accepting to perform this task, you agree to participate in this study; you have the right to stop annotating at any time.In both phases, you will solve 70 tasks, each taking between 15 and 20 minutes.Phase 1:This phase consists of solving two types of tasks that we explain below (Task 1 and Task 2). You will be solving 50 tasks in total; each task is expected to take a maximum of 20 minutes to complete.Task 1:Task context. Law enforcement has identified a forum post we call a Query document (Q document). An investigation has resolved the origin of the post to a particular device such that it must have been written by one of the four potential authors: A, B, C, or D.Â Â Law enforcement need to know if there is evidence to support identifying one of the suspects for further investigation.Task description. Your task is to read the Query document as well as the posts from each author and determine which of the candidate authors is likely to have written the Query documents. In some of these tasks, you will also be given extra explanations of the linguistic, stylistic, and/or semantic features of the Query document, as well as posts from each author.Then, only if this information is given, you will have to answer a set of questions on the quality of explanations.Task 2:Task context. Same as Task 1 contextTask description. This time, you will be presented with an AI agentâ€™s prediction of the Query document's author and the machine-generated explanation that justifies this prediction. Your task is to judge different aspects of the explanation you just saw with respect to the prediction.Annotation PlatformOn the annotation platform, click on the â€œAuthor Attribution Explanationâ€ project. You will then be prompted with a summary of the instructions, and then you can start the evaluation. The total 50 tasks are composed of 10 sets of 5 tasks each, sequentially presented to you. Each set consists of the same Query and Author documents. The first task in the set consists of you solving the Type 1 task without any provided explanations. The second and third tasks in the set consist of you solving the Type 1 task but with explanations provided by two systems (describing the documentsâ€™ writing style and the overall similarity). The fourth and fifth tasks are of Type 2, where we additionally show the AI agent prediction by the two systems, and you have to answer questions regarding the prediction.Noe: More details on this Phase can be found in the Phase 1 Study Instruction and Info Sheet in the attachments.Phase 2:For each task, you will be presented with a query document and four candidate documents, along with the AIâ€™s prediction of the author of the query document with explanations of the decision. Then, you will reason about the AIâ€™s prediction on a follow-up document. You are to guess what the AI would predict.
